exposure: obstetric conditions (e.g., chronic medical conditions, cesarean section, preeclampsia/HELLP)
neonatal conditions (e.g., prematurity, Apgar score less than seven after 5 min, need for respiratory support)
outcome: early skin-to-skin contact (SSC) within six hours after birth
cohort: Mother-infant pairs admitted to Departments of Obstetrics and Neonatology, including 186 mothers (median age 32) and 208 infants (median gestational age 33.36 weeks).
finding: Cesarean section, prematurity, Apgar scores less than seven after 5 minutes, and need for respiratory support were negatively associated with the initiation of early skin-to-skin contact within six hours after birth.
mod_finding: Both emergency and elective cesarean sections were associated with lower odds of early skin-to-skin contact compared to women without cesarean sections.
gest_age: Infants with a median gestational age of 33.36 weeks, including preterm, extremely preterm, and term infants.
